Now make the inclined plane move uniformly horizontally to the left with speed v through a distance l. (The object and the inclined plane are relatively at rest.) Which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The total work done by the inclined plane body on the object is 0

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the inclined plane is placed on the horizontal ground; on the right side, an inclined plane with inclination angle θ and the block on the inclined plane are drawn; on the left side, dashed lines/another position are used to indicate the corresponding position after the inclined plane translates, and the block is still near the same position relative to the inclined plane. A double-headed arrow above the figure marks the horizontal distance l between the two positions, indicating that the inclined plane as a whole has translated a distance l in the horizontal direction, and the block translates together with the inclined plane, with its height unchanged. Then reason: The problem states that the inclined plane moves uniformly horizontally to the left with speed v, and that the object and the inclined plane are relatively at rest, so the block also undergoes uniform horizontal motion relative to the ground. The initial and final speeds of the block are the same, so the change in kinetic energy ΔK=0; the displacement of the block is horizontal and its height is unchanged, so the work done by gravity W_G=0. Apply the work-energy theorem to the block: the sum of the work done by gravity and the work done by the force of the inclined plane body on the object is equal to the change in kinetic energy, namely W_G+W_inclined plane=ΔK=0. Substituting W_G=0 gives W_inclined plane=0. Therefore, the total work done by the inclined plane body on the object is 0.
